title: Customer Journey Heuristic QBR Onramp Lab
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight, beachhead-style QBR template (we call it an "Onramp Lab") designed for strategic accounts that are >6 months into production and heading toward a renewal conversation within 90 days. The emphasis is on validating the customer success hypothesis using customer-journey heuristics rather than just metrics: surface friction, value inflection points, and decision owner alignment.

Audience
- CSM (lead facilitator)
- Solutions engineer or technical lead (data/metrics owner)
- Customer: 1 executive sponsor + 1 product/ops owner + 1 technical stakeholder

Expected outcomes (60–75 minute session)
- Shared diagnosis: agreed top 3 adoption blockers and 2 wins
- Action plan with owners and dates (sprintable)
- Renewal posture signal (green/amber/red + rationale)
- Follow-up workshop scheduled (if needed) to address tech debt or integration items

Pre-Read (send 3 days before)
- 1-page scorecard: usage trend, latency (P50/P95), error rate, cost per 1k tokens, model mix by route
- Recent incident timeline (last 90 days) with remediation status
- Current contract snapshot: renewal date, committed capacity, overage patterns
- Link to shared playbook draft and open Jira list

Agenda (75m)
0–5m: Welcome & frame (CSM)
- Quick norms: timebox, decision ledger, parking lot
- Objective: validate where we believe the product is delivering value vs where it's frictioning adoption

5–20m: Customer journey walk-through (Customer + CSM)
- Customer narrates top 3 workflows where Redwood inference is mission-critical
- Cues for customer: frequency, who uses it, business metric tied to success, current pain

20–35m: Data-backed reality check (SE)
- Present the 1-page scorecard and 2 signal deep-dive (e.g., route A cost spike, route B latency increase during peak)
- Highlight any regressions from last eval set or failing prompts identified in QA harness

35–50m: Hypothesis workshop (facilitated)
- Using heuristic cards (value, friction, viability) quickly vote top 3 hypotheses (sticky notes or Zoom reaction)
- Facilitation script: use the question "If this is fixed, what business metric moves and by how much?" Repeat for each hypothesis

50–65m: Action mapping & owners (CSM + SE)
- Translate hypotheses into sprintable actions (owner, success criteria, due date)
- Capture quick wins that can be shipped in 1–2 sprints and blockers needing engineering time

65–75m: Renewal posture & next steps (exec + CSM)
- Call out renewal signal: green/amber/red with 2-line rationale
- Schedule a 30-day check-in and assign who will run it

Facilitation script / cues (practical)
- Opening line: "We’re here to test our assumptions—what we need from you is truth, not praise."
- If debate stalls: use the data point from the scorecard and ask "Which metric would settle this debate?"
- For execs: surface impact in $ or % of pipeline if possible (e.g., "this feature reduces manual review time by X%")
- Parking lot: anything requiring >2 engineering days goes into a follow-up workshop template

Pre-call checklist for CSM (actionable, checklist-style)
- [ ] Confirm attendees + role map (exec, product, tech) 72 hours out
- [ ] Dispatch pre-read and confirm receipt 72 hours out
- [ ] Pull scorecard: DAU/WAU for routes, P50/P95 latency, 90d error rate, tokens per session, top 10 failing prompts
- [ ] Export last 90 days incident timeline and status (SRE/SE)
- [ ] Confirm demo env or recordings for journey walk-through
- [ ] Create a Miro board (or Google Slide) with heuristic cards ready
- [ ] Create Jira Epic for the QBR follow-ups and link in doc
- [ ] Prepare renewal snapshot: contract end date, committed capacity, any negotiated credits

Data pulls & definitions (so SE can run them)
- Active seats: unique API keys used in last 30 days
- Route-level throughput: requests/min and tokens/min, 7/30/90d windows
- Cost per 1k tokens: blended internal unit cost for hosted calls + dedicated infra allocation
- Error rate: % requests with >=1 error; include HTTP 5xx and model decode failure counts
- Top failing prompts: failure defined by either error or quality regression flagged in eval suite

Renewal posture thermometer (quick rubric)
- Green: adoption trending up, <2 open P1/P2 blockers, exec sponsor engaged, committed capacity stable
- Amber: adoption flat or mixed, 1–3 medium blockers, exec is non-committal or stretched
- Red: adoption declining or concentrated on a single route, >3 medium/high blockers, potential to shop alternative vendors

Example action tracker (compact)
- Action: "Reduce route-A latency at 95th percentile by 40%" | Owner: SE-Diego | Success criteria: P95 < 300ms for 95% of requests | Due: 2026-01-20 | Jira: JIRA-2984
- Action: "Pilot prefix caching for high-volume route" | Owner: CSM-Avery | Success criteria: 10% token reduction on route | Due: 2025-12-15 | Jira: JIRA-3021

Post-QBR outbound template (send within 24 hours)
Subject: Follow-up + decisions from today’s Onramp Lab
Hi [Customer Exec],
Thanks for the time earlier. Quick summary: top 3 hypotheses we validated, actions we committed, and the renewal posture (green/amber/red + short rationale). Attached: updated 1-page scorecard, action tracker with owners and dates, and link to follow-up workshop agenda.

Notes to self / unresolved questions (working doc flavor)
- We don’t yet have a clean, automated export for tokens-per-session that ties to routes — ask infra to prioritize a small telemetry job
- Decide whether to include a short live demo in the 30-day check-in (pros: tangible; cons: time sink)
- Consider a small clause for dedicated customers: "if availability < 99.5% for two consecutive months, prioritize a fallback rollout" (legal wants to avoid feature in contract without engineering agreement)

Appendix: quick facilitation props
- Heuristic card set (value / friction / viability) – printable A4 9-up
- Quick scoreboard slide template (1 slide, top 5 metrics)
- One-page follow-up workshop agenda (90 minutes)

If this format looks right I’ll spin a version tailored for dedicated customers (emphasis on capacity commitments, incident SLAs) and a separate compact exec-only 30-minute readout template.

-- Avery
(working draft; intended to be editable during run-throughs)
